channel.title: Elias Sorel · new works
channel.description: Open preprints by Elias Sorel (French, with English abstracts) on the living world, matter and the cosmos. Each work has a DOI on Zenodo.

item.title: The Diamond: what vibrates, remembers, illuminates (Vibration · Memory · Light)
item.dc:creator: Elias Sorel
item.description: Le Diamant (The Diamond) follows one question across three levels: are rest, conservation and perception what they appear to be? I · Vibration (thesis): nothing is at rest. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22730664

item.title: The Icosahedron: what layers, is read, resonates (Scale · Perception · Resonance)
item.dc:creator: Elias Sorel
item.description: This text starts from a question: from which scale do we look at the living world? It holds in one sentence, "life is a recommencement at different scales", and measures it in three parts. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23250209

item.title: The octopus: the distributed body
item.dc:creator: Elias Sorel
item.description: Anatomy and physiology of a body without a centre. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22676077

item.title: The mitochondrion: complexity as debt rather than conquest
item.dc:creator: Elias Sorel
item.description: The mitochondrial origin of eukaryotic life. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22918398

item.title: The Big Bang: the blinding glare
item.dc:creator: Elias Sorel
item.description: Observational limits and the inference of a cosmological origin. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22938295

item.title: The tardigrade: survival by withdrawal
item.dc:creator: Elias Sorel
item.description: Cryptobiosis and morphological stasis, read as a displacement of selective pressure. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22920277

item.title: The blob: agreement without a leader
item.dc:creator: Elias Sorel
item.description: Physarum polycephalum: information processing with no one inside. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22870114

item.title: Metaphysical Stones
item.dc:creator: Elias Sorel
item.description: Metaphysical Stones is a collection of fifty-four aphorisms ("stones") that state, to the bone, a single view of reality: the world is better described as movement and relation than as fixed, isolated objects. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22865099
